question: Is the retained Plugin SDK and test-fixture compatibility boundary the intended permanent upgrade path for removing runtime `sessionFile` identity, and is the broad refactor ready to merge after a current-head refresh?
rationale: The protected maintainer label and compatibility-sensitive session-storage transition require a human decision on supported extension contracts and upgrade readiness; automated review cannot choose that long-term boundary safely.

options.title: Proceed after current-head proof
options.body: Rebase, confirm compatibility consumers are limited to the documented legacy/SDK boundary, and attach redacted runtime proof before merging.

options.title: Narrow the compatibility surface
options.body: Split any uncertain Plugin SDK or legacy-marker contract changes into a separately discussed compatibility PR before landing the core teardown.

recommendation.title: Proceed after current-head proof
recommendation.body: Rebase, confirm compatibility consumers are limited to the documented legacy/SDK boundary, and attach redacted runtime proof before merging.
